source.title: Why No One Will Know That Viral Photo is Yours (And What Can Help)
source.author: Chris McGreevy

athena.directive: Establish the Creative Liberation Engine as the definitive, self-sovereign platform for immutable digital asset provenance, empowering creators with undeniable ownership and attribution across all digital landscapes.
athena.rationale: Current attempts to ensure digital asset provenance, such as C2PA, are fundamentally undermined by the lack of incentive for large social media platforms to preserve metadata, leading to widespread creator disattribution. Perceptual hashing (pHash) presents a technically superior approach by making the image itself the source of truth, resilient to common modifications. However, pHash requires a robust, self-sovereign infrastructure to realize its full potential. The Creative Liberation Engine, guided by its constitutional mandate for sovereignty and complete implementations, is uniquely positioned to architect and deploy such a system, providing creators with a reliable, owned solution for proving authorship and securing attribution.

options.title: Self-Sovereign Provenance Network for Digital Assets
options.description: Architect and implement a decentralized, Creative Liberation Engine-owned network where creators can register unique perceptual hashes (pHashes) of their digital assets. This network will serve as an authoritative, immutable ledger for proof of creation and ownership, enabling automated attribution verification without reliance on mutable metadata or third-party platforms. It will offer an API for external verification and potentially a user-facing DApp for direct interaction.
options.tradeoffs: Requires significant upfront infrastructure development and ongoing maintenance. Preventing hash collisions and ensuring cryptographic integrity are complex challenges. Initial adoption will depend on convincing creators to actively register their work with a new, independent platform.

options.title: Hybrid Provenance Gateway and Verification Service
options.description: Develop a comprehensive Creative Liberation Engine service that acts as a gateway for digital assets. It will support both C2PA metadata ingestion and validation, alongside automatic pHash generation and registration within a private, secure Creative Liberation Engine ledger. This service would provide an API for content creators and platforms to submit assets, and a public-facing verification portal for checking provenance against both C2PA and pHash records.
options.tradeoffs: Still partially reliant on the limited adoption and integrity of C2PA standards, which have proven ineffective at scale. While providing a robust internal ledger, it doesn't fully embrace a decentralized, self-sovereign network for the pHash component as the primary source of truth, potentially limiting its long-term impact.

options.title: Autonomous Attribution and Rights Enforcement Agent
options.description: Deploy an advanced AI agent, powered by the Creative Liberation Engine, capable of autonomously monitoring public digital spaces (social media, image boards, etc.) for unregistered instances of assets whose pHashes are registered with the Creative Liberation Engine. Upon detection, the agent would automatically initiate attribution requests or, where appropriate, digital rights management claims on behalf of the registered creator, adhering to pre-defined legal frameworks.
options.tradeoffs: Requires sophisticated AI development for accurate image recognition and legal compliance across various jurisdictions. Faces significant challenges with platform terms of service and potential legal pushback from social media giants. Ethical considerations around automated enforcement and potential for false positives are high.

options.title: Immutable Ledger for Digital Asset Fingerprints
options.description: Leverage blockchain technology to create an immutable, transparent ledger specifically for registering and timestamping digital asset pHashes. The Creative Liberation Engine would architect and maintain this ledger, providing a trustless and verifiable record of creation. This would ensure that once a pHash is registered, its association with a creator and timestamp cannot be altered or disputed.
options.tradeoffs: High complexity and resource intensity associated with blockchain development, deployment, and ongoing maintenance. Potential scalability issues for extremely high volumes of registrations, leading to increased transaction costs or slower processing. User experience might be more complex for non-technical creators.

options.title: Creator-Owned 'Proof of Creation' Decentralized Application
options.description: Design and build a user-friendly decentralized application (DApp) that empowers individual creators to directly manage the provenance of their digital assets. Creators would use the DApp to upload assets, automatically generate and register pHashes on a public, immutable ledger (potentially blockchain-based), and receive verifiable 'proof of creation' tokens or certificates. The DApp would also provide tools for creators to share their work with embedded provenance links.
options.tradeoffs: Requires significant effort in user experience design for a decentralized application to ensure broad accessibility. Adoption is dependent on creator willingness to engage with DApp technology, which still has a learning curve for many. The underlying ledger's scalability and cost would be a critical consideration.

options.title: Open-Source pHash Standard and Reference Implementation
options.description: Focus on developing and open-sourcing a robust, highly performant pHash generation and comparison library, along with a comprehensive API and documentation, to serve as a universal standard for digital asset fingerprinting. The Creative Liberation Engine would position itself as a key contributor to the open-source ecosystem, fostering widespread adoption by third-party applications and platforms.
options.tradeoffs: While beneficial for the broader ecosystem by promoting a standard, this approach does not align with the Creative Liberation Engine's constitutional mandate for self-sovereign, owned solutions. It delegates the core problem-solving and infrastructure development to external entities, reducing direct control over the provenance network's integrity and long-term vision.
